guards: Condition/ADC/SBB consumers reject unmodeled or undefined flags
Architecturally masked-zero shifts and rotates preserve prior flags; narrow full-cycle rotates refuse flag consumers
SAR by1 supplies OF0; BSR supplies ZF and conservatively refuses zero-source execution
Out-of-word register offsets for memory BT/BTS refuse execution; in-word and register-modulo forms remain supported
Unsupported narrow one-operand multiply/divide and 16-bit double-shift forms refuse execution
Non-REX.W SSE integer conversions and ambiguous high-byte extension sources refuse execution
limits: The decoder and historical packet records are unchanged; accepting a decode alone is not an execution correctness claim
The comparison establishes equality on five stated workloads, not hardware ISA equivalence or support for arbitrary programs
Direct Python inspection of flag attributes must first check unsupported_flags; instruction consumers enforce the check automatically
Floating operations assume default masked SSE exceptions and round-to-nearest; MXCSR and other FP modes are not modeled
Integer parity and several shift/rotate/architecturally undefined flags are deliberately not supplied
